memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But now we have lost our appetite; we never see anything but this manna! The manna was like coriander seed and looked like resin. The people went around gathering it, and then ground it in a hand mill or crushed it in a mortar. They cooked it in a pot or made it into loaves. And it tasted like something made with olive oil. When the dew settled on the camp at night, the manna also came down. — Num 11:6-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"We never see anything but this manna!" What a sad sentence. The manna was a daily miracle — bread from heaven, appearing faithfully with the morning dew, enough for every single person. Yet familiarity had bred contempt. The wonder had become boring.

This is one of the quiet dangers of the spiritual life. God's mercies come to us "new every morning," so steadily and dependably that we stop noticing them. The very reliability of God's kindness can make us take it for granted. We yawn at gifts we once would have wept for.

Look at how the writer lingers over the manna — its taste, its texture, how it could be ground and baked and cooked. He wants us to see how good it actually was. God had not given them something dull; He had given them something wonderful that they had learned to despise.

Jesus later called Himself the true bread that came down from heaven, the One the manna was pointing to all along. When our appetite for spiritual things grows dull — when prayer feels routine and Scripture feels flat — the answer is not new experiences but fresh eyes. Ask God to help you taste again how good He is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What blessing from God have you stopped noticing because it is so familiar?
2. Has any part of your walk with God started to feel "boring"?
3. How can you recover a sense of wonder at God's daily provision?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for growing bored with Your good gifts. Open my eyes to see Your daily mercies afresh, and give me a renewed hunger for Christ, the true Bread from heaven. Amen.
